I’ll check the current Pitch export flow so the steps match the interface you’re seeing.

In Pitch, use the **Share** button in the top-right—not the hamburger menu that’s open in your screenshot.

1. Click **Share** (top right).
2. Choose **Export**.
3. Select **High Quality PDF** (best for sending/printing) or **Compressed PDF** (smaller file).
4. Pitch downloads the PDF to your browser’s normal Downloads folder.

Shortcut: press `⌘ K`, type **Export**, then choose the PDF format.

Note: videos, GIFs, and animations become static thumbnails in the PDF; on Pitch’s free plan, the exported file includes a small Pitch watermark. [Pitch’s export guide](https://help.pitch.com/en/articles/3551638-export-a-presentation-to-pdf)
Where is the share button, I don't see it.
Your screenshot helps: the usual Share control isn’t visible in that editor header, so I’m checking the alternative export entry point in Pitch.

It isn’t visible in your screenshot—likely because this is a deck **shared with you** (shown below “harve/y”), and you may not have permission to export/share it.

Try the export shortcut directly:

1. Press `⌘ K`.
2. Type **Export**.
3. Choose **Export presentation** → **High Quality PDF**.

If **Export** doesn’t appear, ask the deck owner to either export it for you or give you sharing/export permission. The Share button would normally be in the top-right header, near your avatar/play controls.

content.text:
Initial read: the strongest story is not “we used an LLM to negotiate.” It is “we turn every offer into a comparable total-cost decision, show the evidence, and keep the model outside the authority boundary.” The live lab already supports that story through experiment comparison, score history, and memory, but it currently has no seeded runs on this local preview, so it cannot be the only proof surface.

For three minutes, I recommend a six-slide arc: stakes → full-cost insight → decision architecture → one recorded replay → measured evidence → live lab/close. The screen demo should be a short, rehearsed reveal, with a slide-based replay ready as an instant fallback. That keeps the product central without risking a blank state or network timing.

Those measure different moments/configurations, so I won’t combine them or present a cherry-picked number.
